subject: maths
question: The total surface area of a hemisphere is 4,158 m². If the radius of the hemisphere becomes one-third of itself, then what will be the new curved surface area of the hemisphere? (Use π = 22/7)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area (TSA) of hemisphere = 3πr² = 4158 m².

⇒ πr² = 4158 ÷ 3 = 1386 m².

New radius (R) = r/3. New Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πR².

⇒ New CSA = 2π(r/3)² = (2/9) × πr².

⇒ New CSA = (2/9) × 1386 = 2 × 154 = 308 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 308 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of hemisphere = 4158 m²

New radius (R) = Original radius (r) ÷ 3

**Formula Used:**

TSA of hemisphere = 3πr²

CSA of hemisphere = 2πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b7dde904df6476c80c8923307dba44deb583530f3d3b89378d857206eb87be29.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3 × (22/7) × r² = 4158

⇒ (66/7) × r² = 4158

⇒ r² = (4158 × 7) ÷ 66

⇒ r² = 63 × 7 = 441

⇒ r = √441 = 21 m

Now, new radius R = 21 ÷ 3 = 7 m

⇒ New CSA = 2 × π × R²

⇒ New CSA = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 7

⇒ New CSA = 2 × 22 × 7

⇒ New CSA = 44 × 7 = 308 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 308 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Hemisphere

The amount of space occupied by a hemisphere is given by the formula V = (2/3)πr³.

Surface Area of a Sphere

A sphere has only one surface area (TSA = CSA), which is calculated as 4πr².

Volume of a Sphere

The volume of a complete sphere is exactly double that of a hemisphere: V = (4/3)πr³.</p
